```{r} 
#| echo: true

# setup
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(1)
x <- 1:100
e = rnorm(100,mean=0, sd = 0.2)
y <- sin(x/10) + e


custom_lowess = function(x, y, f){
  num_samples = ceiling(f * length(x))  # Value of k

  smoothed_values = numeric(length(x))  # Ensuring i can access the smoothed values outside of the loop
  
  for (i in 1:length(x)) {
    distances = abs(x - x[i])  # from the vector x subtract specifically the value at point i from every point and take the absolute value
    
    closest_indices = order(distances)[1:num_samples]  # This returns the indexes of the nearest neighbors
    
    # This next step ensures that the matrices are all conformable
    
    neighbors_x = x[closest_indices]  # Select x values of nearest neighbors
    neighbors_y = y[closest_indices]  # Select y values of nearest neighbors
    
    max_dist = max(distances[closest_indices])  
    
    # Using the formula Jake gave calculate the distances before converting it into a diagonal matrix
    w = ifelse(distances[closest_indices] > max_dist, 0, 
               (1 - (abs(distances[closest_indices]) / max_dist)^3)^3)
    
    w_diag = diag(w) 
    
    x_df = cbind(1, neighbors_x)  # converting the x matrix into a design matrix
    y_df = matrix(neighbors_y, ncol = 1)
    
    # Actual beta hat calculation
    beta_hat <- solve(t(x_df) %*% w_diag %*% x_df) %*% t(x_df) %*% w_diag %*% y_df
    
    # Predict smoothed value at x[i]
    smoothed_values[i] = beta_hat[1] + beta_hat[2] * x[i]  
  }
  
  return(smoothed_values)
}

# Create a data frame with original points and smoothed values
df <- data.frame(
  x = x,
  y = y,
  my_lowess = custom_lowess(x, y, 0.2),
  built_in_lowess = lowess(x, y, f = 0.2)$y  # Extract the smoothed y values
)

# Plot using ggplot
ggplot(df, aes(x = x)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = y), color = "gray", alpha = 0.5) +  # Original data points
  geom_line(aes(y = my_lowess, color = "Custom LOWESS"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = built_in_lowess, color = "Built-in LOWESS"), linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of Custom and Built-in LOWESS",
    x = "X Values",
    y = "Smoothed Y Values",
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Custom LOWESS" = "blue", "Built-in LOWESS" = "red")) +
  theme_minimal()
```
